body:
Firefox at least sends `Range: bytes=0-`.
The original reason AIUI was to see whether the server supported range requests.  That does seem to work in most cases but is not guaranteed because the server could choose to ignore and respond with 200.
Subsequently `bytes=0-` has been useful to indicate that servers can reply with a questionable incomplete range, and some do.
I don't know why Firefox does not use `bytes=0-<max-buffer-size>` instead, but I guess there is a fingerprinting issue here.
